question: Will Carlos Alcaraz win the 2026 Men's US Open?
rules:
The 2026 U.S. Open tennis tournament is scheduled for August 23 - September 13, 2026.

This market will resolve to the player that wins the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed player to win the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament per the rules of the tournament, the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament is cancelled, postponed after October 31, 2026, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Open (https://www.usopen.org/index.html); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

evidence.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz confirmed Thursday that he will compete at the 2026 US Open, announcing his return from a right wrist injury that has sidelined him since April. Alcaraz posted a 22-3 record in the first four months of the 2026 season, winning titles at the Australian Open and in Doha. His Australian Open trophy made him the youngest man in history to complete the career Grand Slam, winning a men's singles title at all four majors at the age of 22.

Alcaraz has not played a match since 14 April, when he beat Otto Virtanen in his opener at the Barcelona Open Banc Sabadell. In recent days, the Spaniard has shared a court in Murcia with Holger Rune. Alcaraz will touch down at Flushing Meadows without an official match under his belt since April and go straight into a best-of-five-set tournament.

The provisional schedule has been released ahead of the fourth and final Grand Slam of the season at the US Open. The schedule lists the start of ATP singles first-round play on Sunday 30 August and the ATP singles final on Sunday 13 September.

NEW YORK (AP) — Top-ranked Jannik Sinner withdrew from the U.S. Open on Friday, unable to recover from a right knee injury that has sidelined him since winning the Wimbledon title. Sinner beat Alexander Zverev last month for his second straight title at the All England Club, but then pulled out of the hard-court tournaments in Montreal and Cincinnati that serve as a warmup for the U.S. Open. He wrote Friday that he won't be ready when the main draw begins on Aug. 30.

BENGALURU, Aug 26 (Reuters) – Carlos Alcaraz returns from a nearly five-month injury layoff for his U.S. Open title defence with little match practice but no shortage of expectation as the flamboyant Spaniard bids to win a third title in New York.

evidence.excerpt: The German comes to Flushing Meadows as a Grand Slam champion for the first time, having broken the Sinner-Alcaraz stranglehold on majors with his French Open triumph in June, ending a run in which the pair shared the previous nine majors. The 29-year-old then reached his first Wimbledon final, where his impressive run was only stopped by Sinner, extending his losing streak against the Italian to 10 matches. Questions remain about his form after an underwhelming North American hard-court swing, which saw him fall in the first round in Toronto before reaching the fourth round in Cincinnati, where he squandered a match point in a loss to American Tommy Paul.

Carlos Alcaraz ha decidido darse un respiro este miércoles y no saltar a las pistas de entrenamiento del US Open. 134 días después, este martes jugó dos partidos consecutivos en el dobles mixto del US Open de la mano de Serena Williams. El jugador murciano, en su regreso a las pistas, sumó un total de 1 hora y 55 minutos a un nivel relativamente alto.
